prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the right agency depends on your goals, budget, industry, timeline and whether you need brand strategy, performance marketing (PPC/paid social), SEO, content, product/UX, or a mix.

Quick questions so I can recommend specific agencies:
- What’s your main goal? (e.g., brand awareness, lead generation, e‑commerce revenue, app installs)
- Monthly/annual marketing budget range?
- Industry (SaaS, fintech, e‑commerce, healthcare, consumer, etc.)?
- Do you prefer a big agency (full service, enterprise-level) or a boutique/performance shop?
- Do you need ongoing services or a short-term project?

If you want immediate, general guidance, here are common choices by strength:

- Large/full-service & creative (brand + digital product)
  - AKQA — experience design, digital product and brand-driven campaigns.
  - R/GA — innovation, integrated campaigns, product + marketing strategy.
  - Goodby Silverstein & Partners — creative-driven brand campaigns.

- Performance / growth-focused (PPC, paid social, CRO)
  - 3Q Digital (San Francisco-founded) — paid search, social, analytics, CRO.
  - Smaller boutique growth agencies — often better for fast experimentation and lower budgets.

- SEO / Content specialists
  - Boutique SEO/content agencies or freelancers — good when organic growth is priority.

How to choose and vet agencies:
- Ask for relevant case studies and measurable KPIs (CPA, LTV, ROAS, organic traffic % increase).
- Check client roster and references, especially from companies like yours.
- Confirm tooling and reporting cadence (analytics, dashboards, access to raw data).
- Look at team composition and who will work on your account (senior vs. junior).
- Trial with a small pilot project before committing long term.

If you tell me your goals, budget and industry I’ll shortlist 4–6 San Francisco agencies tailored to your needs (with strengths, expected cost range, and sample questions to ask each).
